title: Casper and the Blue Hour
premise: Jude Amberdale, a bridge inspector whose marriage has quietly calcified, hears an unrecorded song on the radio — one written by their late friend Casper and never performed — and is pulled into the memory-world of the blue hour it describes. Inside the song, Jude must confront the unfinished goodbye to Casper, the silences that hollowed their marriage to Priya, and the small corruptions of power that let them decide what everyone else got to know. As the demolition date for the bridge Jude has inspected for twenty years approaches, the song's world begins to collapse in step with the concrete. The book ends at dawn on demolition day: Jude says Casper's name aloud at last, Priya stands beside them holding the inventory of unsaid things finally spoken, and the bridge falls as the two of them walk forward into an ordinary, unglamorous, chosen morning.
about_author: Isandro Iversen is a former municipal structural engineer who left the profession after fifteen years to write about the weight of things that hold and things that don't. They live in a coastal town where the fog arrives early and stay up for the blue hour most nights.

chapters.title: Expansion Joints
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A day of routine bridge inspection rendered in obsessive, tender detail, intercut with the silent choreography of Jude and Priya's evening — two people fluent in logistics and mute in feeling. The emotional beat is quiet dread: Jude inventories cracks in steel and in speech, and admits to no one that the two ledgers have become the same book.

chapters.title: The Unrecorded
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Driving home at dusk, a radio station plays a song Jude has never heard and knows entirely — Casper's song, written the winter before he died, played for no one. The car fills with the blue hour itself. The emotional beat is vertigo: grief arriving not as memory but as a physical place Jude is suddenly standing inside.

chapters.title: Casper's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, inside the song. The blue hour world reconstructs Casper's apartment the night the song was written — cigarettes, a broken amp, Casper alive and annoyed at being interrupted. Jude cannot say why they're here. The beat is aching comedy turning to panic: Casper doesn't know he's dead, and Jude's tongue won't form the sentence.

chapters.title: What Priya Kept
chapters.summary: Priya's POV, waking world. While Jude sleeps, Priya finds the notebook — twenty years of inventory: every unsaid thing, catalogued in Jude's handwriting, including the truth about the night Casper died and what Jude chose not to tell her. The beat is cold clarity: Priya realizes she has been married to an archivist of omissions, and that she appears in it mostly as a silence.

chapters.title: The Blue Hour Rules
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, inside the song. Jude learns the world's logic: it runs on things unsaid; each truth spoken aloud collapses a piece of it. Casper, sensing the edges fraying, asks the question Jude fled twenty years ago. The beat is rising tension — honesty has a price, and Jude begins to suspect the demolition date and the song's ending are the same appointment.

chapters.title: Inspection Report
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, waking world. Jude falsifies nothing but delays the final report on the bridge, buying the song more time — a small, corruptible power wielded for a private grief, and Jude knows it. Priya, holding the notebook, says only: 'Take me with you next time.' The beat is the marriage's first crack of light: an ultimatum shaped like an invitation.

chapters.title: Duet
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, both worlds bleeding together. Priya enters the blue hour with Jude; Casper meets the wife he only ever heard about, and the three of them argue in a kitchen that is also a bridge deck at dusk. The beat is cathartic rupture: Priya says her unsaid things to Casper's face, and the song's melody visibly fractures.

chapters.title: The Corruption of Small Powers
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The blue hour turns: Casper's ghost-world offers Jude a bargain — stay inside the song, where the goodbye never has to finish, where Priya never has to be told everything. Jude recognizes the temptation as the same muscle that let them control the marriage's silences for twenty years. The beat is the dark night: Jude almost says yes.

chapters.title: Out Loud
chapters.summary: Jude and Priya's shared POV, climax in both worlds at once. On the bridge, hours before demolition, Jude speaks Casper's death aloud — the truth, the guilt, the whole inventory — while the song collapses around them, verse by verse, and Casper finally hears it, finally answers. The beat is devastating release: the goodbye performed properly, at last, with witnesses.

chapters.title: Demolition Date
chapters.summary: Priya's POV, resolution. Dawn. The bridge comes down on schedule; Jude watches without flinching, the notebook closed, its last page blank. Priya and Jude eat breakfast at a diner with bad coffee and talk about nothing important — and the nothing is the point. The beat is earned ordinariness: grief finished rather than managed, and two people choosing to begin saying things out loud.
